label: neiso 43 closeout
definition: neiso-43 closes NEISO: the neiso-41 keeper recipe (rebuilt generic reliability-floor engine, gas-hub-basis-daily overlay, EIA-930 hydro budget) plus a post-solve ORDC scarcity-price overlay with ISO-NE-grounded parameters (VOLL $2000 = Tariff III.1.10.1A offer cap, MCL 1200 MW = Millstone 3 largest contingency, sigma 900 MW = ISO-NE PAF Study 2022); the overlay adds a reserve-shortage adder to econ_prices for capacity economics but leaves dispatch/LP prices unchanged. C1 fuel-mix now passes outright; the remaining C2 2025 gas +2.8% is an accepted preliminary-vintage caveat (EIA-930 gas-cell geothermal/biomass fold-in, the same categorization issue as the C1 exceptions on complete vintages, not a dispatch error), and the C3c price-tail / C5b/C5c storage caveats trace to the LP's oil-parity cap on cold-hour prices, which the overlay prices for capacity value but does not lift out of the persisted LP prices that drive C3c/C5b/C5c; C6 governance passes. RE-GATED 2026-07-04 under the extended rubric: C3b price-shape is a soft FAIL (2024 NRMSE 0.160), C7 diurnal shape FAILS (CT_PEAKER profile r 0.57-0.90 with off-peak CV ratio 0.0-0.02, the flat-floor signature, across all three years, plus 2023 ST_GAS r 0.608 / CV ratio 14.4), and C8 forced-energy share FAILS (CT_PEAKER 44.0-55.3% forced 2023-2025 on a tiny <0.15 TWh/yr class; rebuilt floors exclude the P1-dependent RA bridge, so these are lower bounds). Determination NOT-YET (deciding criteria: C3b price-shape, C7 diurnal shape, C8 forced-energy share, all outright FAILs).
